title: Spectral Dispersion Analysis Lab
description: The user operates a virtual chemistry lab where the AnisotropyBarnLamp serves as an adjustable broadband light source illuminating a prism apparatus (DispersionTest). The user must calibrate the lamp intensity, angle, and wavelength filters across multiple coupled parameters to separate a target spectral pattern, while conserving total photon energy across all output channels. Full undo/redo support lets the user backtrack through their calibration steps.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a chemistry spectral analysis lab. Load AnisotropyBarnLamp.glb positioned at (-3,1,0) as the lab light source and DispersionTest.glb at (0,0.8,0) as the prism/dispersion apparatus on a lab bench. Use a PerspectiveCamera at (0,3,6) with OrbitControls. Add ambient light (0.15) and a point light parented to the lamp model. Create an HTML overlay panel with these controls: (1) Lamp Intensity slider 0-100%, (2) Lamp Angle rotary dial -45 to +45 degrees rotating the lamp around Y-axis, (3) Three wavelength filter toggles (Red/Green/Blue) that enable or disable spectral channels, (4) Prism Rotation slider 0-360 degrees rotating the DispersionTest model around Y, (5) Aperture Width slider controlling a visible slit plane between lamp and prism. Implement energy conservation: total output energy across RGB readout bars must equal lamp intensity multiplied by active filter count divided by 3, redistributed by prism angle. Display three colored energy bars on the right side showing per-channel output. The target goal is displayed as three specific RGB energy values the user must match within 5% tolerance. When all three channels match, show a success banner. Implement a full undo/redo stack (Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y and on-screen buttons) tracking every parameter change as a state snapshot. Visually connect lamp to prism with three colored line segments (red, green, blue) whose opacity reflects each channel energy, originating from the lamp and fanning out past the prism at angles determined by prism rotation. The point light color should blend based on active filters. Require 10-14 deliberate steps to solve: toggling filters, adjusting intensity, rotating prism, setting aperture, and fine-tuning angle. Render loop updates beam visuals and energy bars each frame. Style the UI with a dark lab-themed background.
